messages.text: ok sketch looks good. 'library catalog' is a great north star. i'm actually building the endpoint now, so we can sync on tokens soon?
yes please! sending the token list right now so you can see the hex values. also, i'm using Inter for everything. it's clean and doesn't have that 'tech startup' vibe we want to avoid
turquoise accent: 600 for text/links (#0d9488), 500 for lines/dividers (#14b8a6), 100 for soft washes behind cards (#ccfbf1). contrast for the 600 on white is 4.9:1 so it passes aa easily
noted. 4.9:1 is safe for mobile. i'm setting up the CSS variables in index.css. are we using a type scale? i was thinking 12/14/16/20/28 to keep it tight
perfect scale. 12px for the 'rarity score' tags, 14 for body text, 16 for cards, 20 for section headers, 28 for the user's name at the top. keep line-heights around 1.5
copying that into the config. one question: do we need a dark mode for this? it adds complexity to the token setup and i'm trying to keep the css minimal for the demo
no! definitely not. white space is our friend here. let's just nail the light mode. less css means faster loads too, which i know you care about more than i do
haha fair. speed > aesthetics usually, but your 'library' vibe is winning so far. i'm using the 500 turquoise for the border of the 'shared concept' chips. does that work visually?
yes! it'll look like a subtle highlighter pen mark. just make sure the text inside those chips is the ink color (like #111827 or similar) so it pops against the teal border
got it. i'll push a branch with the tokens and the endpoint soon. you can pull it in and see how the json maps to your chip design
awesome, i'll be waiting. this is going to look so clean. thanks for being so specific about the contrast, it usually gets skipped until it's too late
